upstream.observed_serializer: Command preview only transforms double quote to apostrophe and is inserted with printf into a hand-built JSON line; hint is inserted without general JSON escaping.

hypothesis_under_test: The production shell-built JSONL remains valid JSON for arbitrary command/hint text admitted by the wrapper.

counterexample.environment: isolated local deterministic Linux container; donor falsifier only
counterexample.input_class: command contains an actual newline and backslash-sensitive text; hint contains a backslash
counterexample.method: Apply the same command-preview transformation and printf JSON structure used by the audited production wrapper, then parse the rendered line with a standard JSON parser.
counterexample.observed_failure: Invalid control character caused by unescaped newline in the JSON string; backslash-bearing text is also not generally escaped.

result.finding: The production shell serialization pattern is not a robust canonical JSON serializer for arbitrary command/hint text.

f2_architecture_delta.recommended_rule: Resource/tool evidence must be serialized by a typed JSON/JCS-capable serializer; never construct canonical evidence JSON by interpolating untrusted strings into printf/shell templates.
recommended_fields: exact tool/effect digest or immutable reference
bounded human-readable preview as non-authoritative projection
f2_architecture_delta.authority_boundary: Malformed telemetry must fail closed as DEGRADED/UNKNOWN coverage rather than silently disappear or become canonical evidence.

counterhypothesis_remaining: If F2 guarantees a much narrower command/hint alphabet before logging, a simple serializer could be safe within that declared domain; such a restriction would need explicit validation and still should not replace the existing typed canonicalization path.
next_exact_action: Preserve this as a negative donor result and require any future F2 ResourceEnvelope implementation to reuse typed canonical serialization. A separate E3 may test AgentCgroup's no-root peak-memory measurement against a child workload with known peak allocation.
